q: What is the standard height of a kitchen counter?
n: Kitchen counters are typically about 85–90 cm high. The item's 85 (cm) suits shorter users. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (kitchens); Panero & Zelnik.

q: What is the comfortable height of a dining chair?
n: A comfortable dining chair seat height is about 0.45 m. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the minimum length of a meeting table for six persons?
n: A meeting table for six (three per side) is at least about 1,400 mm long, giving about 0.45–0.60 m per person. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (dining and conference tables).

q: What is the minimum size of a two-seater sofa?
n: A two-seater sofa is at least about 700 × 1,400 mm. The size fits two seats of about 600 mm each plus arms. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: What is the area requirement for the smallest stand-alone gas range available in the market?
n: The smallest freestanding gas ranges are about 600 × 600 mm, so 0.36 m². Source: Manufacturer data; Neufert, Architects' Data (kitchens).

q: What is the typical depth of a wardrobe cabinet?
n: Wardrobe cabinets are typically about 60 cm deep, enough for clothes on hangers. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data; Panero & Zelnik.

q: What is the total area of a common nightstand table?
n: A common nightstand is about 450 × 450 mm, so 0.45 × 0.45 ≈ 0.203 m². Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (bedroom furniture).

q: What is the standard depth of a kitchen sink and range?
n: Kitchen sinks and ranges sit in the standard 600 mm counter depth. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (kitchens).

q: How high should an accessible lavatory be?
n: An accessible lavatory is mounted at 0.80 m, with knee clearance below. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), toilets.

q: What is the ideal size of a dining table (one side) for four persons?
n: A table for four (two per side) needs about 1.00 m on a side, about 0.50–0.60 m per diner. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (dining).

q: If a dining table for two persons is used, how much width is occupied?
n: A two-person dining set, table plus chairs pulled out, occupies about 1.40 m in width. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (dining space requirements).

q: Which of the following is not a good depth for a fixed countertop?
n: Fixed countertops are about 0.40–0.60 m deep. 0.20 m is too shallow to be useful. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data; Panero & Zelnik.

q: What is the ideal length for one side of an 8-seater dining table?
n: An 8-seater table (four per side) needs about 0.75 m per diner, plus end clearance, so about 3.75 m along each side in the item's layout. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (dining space requirements).

q: What is the ideal size of one side of a square table seating people?
n: The item's square table seating takes about 1.44 m per side, allowing elbow room for each diner at the table. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (dining).

q: What is the minimum width of a corridor serving one side only?
n: A corridor serving one side only must be at least 1.10 m wide. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.

q: What is the minimum clear distance of seats placed back-to-back?
n: Seats placed back-to-back need at least 600 mm clear between them for passage. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the minimum clear distance of a table from the wall?
n: Leave at least 900 mm between a table and a wall for chair pull-out and circulation. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the standard size of a queen bed?
n: In the item's metric standard, a queen bed is 1,500 × 1,900 mm (US queen 60 × 80 in.). Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds); mattress industry sizes.

q: What is the standard width of a queen bed?
n: A queen bed is about 1.50 m (≈60 in.) wide. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data; mattress industry sizes.

q: What is the standard width of a king bed?
n: A king bed is about 1.80 m (≈72–76 in.) wide. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data; mattress industry sizes.

q: What is the total area of a common king-size bed?
n: A common king bed is 1.80 × 1.90 m = 3.42 m². This bed area is used in space planning to size master bedrooms. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds).

q: What is the total area of a common double-size bed?
n: A common double bed is 1.35 × 1.90 m = 2.565 m². Planners use this footprint to lay out bedrooms with circulation around the bed. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds).

q: What is the total area of a common single-size bed?
n: A common single bed is 0.90 × 1.90 m = 1.71 m². This footprint is used to plan children's rooms, dormitories and hotel singles. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds).

q: For alow-cost condominium project, what is the total area of a common king-size bed?
n: A common king bed is 1.80 × 1.90 = 3.42 m² regardless of project type. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds).

q: For a first-class hotel near the beach, what is the total area of a common single-size bed?
n: A common single bed is 0.90 × 1.90 = 1.71 m² regardless of project type. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (beds).

q: What is the size of an element or space relative to the dimensions of the human body?
n: Human scale is the size of an element or space relative to the dimensions of the human body. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is the measurement and study of the size and proportions of the human body?
n: Anthropometrics is the measurement and study of the size and proportions of the human body. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the size an element appears to have relative to elements of known size?
n: Visual scale is the size an element appears to have relative to elements of known size. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What are dimensions taken in a still posture, like sitting or standing?
n: Static (structural) dimensions are taken in a still posture, sitting or standing. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: Which individual space shifts with the situation or interaction?
n: Personal space is a dynamic "bubble" that shifts with the situation and interaction. Source: Sommer, Personal Space; Hall, The Hidden Dimension.

q: A kind of passive ventilation that uses natural forces to pull air through a building is ___.
n: Natural ventilation is passive ventilation driven by natural forces, wind pressure and buoyancy (stack effect), moving air through a building. Source: ASHRAE Handbook, Fundamentals (natural ventilation); Givoni.
